newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium above $1,700 at 14-month LME high.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium above $1,700 at 14-month LME high.

text.p: Aluminium prices broke above the $1,700 a tonne level during Tuesday London Metal Exchange (LME) pre-market trading to hit the highest since December 1995.
Prices touched a high of $1,701 a tonne, up from the overnight kerb close of $1,690.
Traders said aluminium's strength on Tuesday followed a solid performance on Monday, when most base metals in the LME complex were rising.
Investment funds have been buying aluminium, and there has also been good consumer interest in key end-using regions. Metal stocks are falling, with LME inventories dropping 7,725 tonnes on Tuesday.
The market has also been reacting to the possibility of an interruption to Russian exports of metal after Russia's interior minister called for curbs on foreign ownership in the domestic industry.
This could impact on tolling business, as Russian smelters would not be able to fund alumina purchases from Western countries, traders noted.
